what: Checks run by build_moonlight.py for moon-light-2026-06-R1 (MOON-LIT-AS-NOW-PROPOSAL rev 2.1 §3 and §10).

independent.method: DE440 ASCII records 873–891 (EMB, geocentric Moon, Sun, librations) with this script's own Chebyshev evaluator and derivative; EMRAT from header.440; own UTC→TDB from the leap-second kernel's constants; own light-time iteration and Newtonian stellar aberration for the Sun; own 3-1-3 libration rotation and NAIF's fixed PA→ME offset. No SPICE call.
independent.compared: angle between unit vectors, larger of Sun and Earth, at every sample
independent.note: No leap second is scheduled after 2017-01-01 in naif0012.tls; a future one inside the table would shift its later samples by 1 s (about 0.00014° of sub-solar longitude).

june_rotation.note: pxform from the wider PCK byte range (records 21750–21823), rounded as archived (15 decimals).

horizons.horizons_conventions: Apparent quantities at the observer time t: the Moon and its orientation at t − lt (down-leg light time, no aberration); the Sun as seen from the Moon at t − lt, apparent (light time and stellar aberration); illuminated fraction from those two directions. Reading the sub-solar point with light time only leaves the residual in sun_without_aberration_deg (about the 20" aberration constant), so that reading is rejected.

catalogue_convention_residual.explanation: The catalogue takes sunlight arriving at the Moon at t (with aberration) and the geometric Earth at t; Horizons ties both to an Earth observer at t, about 1.3 s of light time later than the Moon event. Not judged against the ceilings.

interpolation.rule: spherical interpolation of the rounded samples (as moonlight.js)

source.extract: rows 15 Nov 2026 00:00 UT to 31 Dec 2026 23:00 UT; columns time, phase, subsolar lon/lat, subearth lon/lat, values as published

svs.status: corroboration only; no ceiling; offsets as found
svs.note: SVS publishes 3 decimals of a degree and 2 of a percent and lists DE421. Its page does not state light-time or aberration conventions; the offsets here are against the catalogue conventions.
